Result

I replaced the inherited meter with a different physical construction and obtained an exact finite-duration parity operation, its complete noisy quantum instrument, an entangling-gate calculation, and a concrete noisy error-correction protocol that can consume it.

The central result is stronger than a correct parity bit or preservation of one coherence pair: within the stated effective Hamiltonian, the entire intended output field carries only the parity throughout the operation, both parity sectors retain their internal quantum information, and all three apparatus modes return to vacuum at the endpoint.

The broader objective remains open. I have not established a hardware or total-resource advantage over the strongest existing routes. An equally informed conventional optimizer improves the new construction, and the preparation, control, and fault-reset calculations expose substantial costs.

The complete continuation is preserved here:

10. What this continuation establishes

The principal verification combines ordinary algebra with independent calculations:

Direct substitution proves the finite physical trajectory and output cancellation.
The controlled isometry proves the full superposition/reference statement.
Independent three-mode Fock Lindblad calculations test all six logical coherences, including unequal auxiliary losses. These deliberately use weak signals; the all-amplitude effective-model claim comes from the analytic proof.
Complete instruments pass positivity and trace-preservation checks and are composed into the full CNOT channel.
The subsystem calculation checks all 10,000 ordered error products in the declared correctable family.
The recovery check covers arbitrary faulty-round reports.
The reset envelope has an exact arithmetic certificate compatible with the adopted loss rates.

The strongest retained Astra ingredient is therefore a finite physical construction with an exact all-output instrument and an explicit route into noisy recovery. The conventional optimizer, code, and ancilla competitors are incorporated on their merits.

My scientific assessment is that the operation-level gap has narrowed substantially, while the mission-level cost gap remains unresolved. The decisive comparison now requires a compatible microscopic operating window: two real conditional forces, their bandwidth and parasitic terms, cold preparation, data lifetime during sensing and cleanup, stable calibration, and repeated recovery must jointly outperform an optimized matched-qutrit, flying-cat, or dual-rail route.

The present evidence does not justify choosing the three-mode apparatus over those alternatives. It does provide a precise construction, a strong control-class cost bound, and a complete set of failures that make the remaining comparison concrete.
